subject: Oxford Lane — sudden throughput regression impacting checkout (peering/DNS suspect)
messages:
From: Maya Allen <ops@oxfordlane.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Latency/5xx spike starting ~08:45 PST - checkout failures

Rafael — we're seeing a sudden surge in checkout latency and a spike in 5xx from Redwood-backed inference calls starting ~08:45 PST. Our telemetry shows median latency from our edge to your inference gateway went from ~120ms to ~1.8s and error rate rose to 6% (normally <0.2%).

Impact: user checkout flows timing out, ~12% of purchase attempts failing in the last 30m.

What we've done: we've captured a pcap at our egress and included a short trace in the attached tar (pcap summary + flame graph). It looks like repeated DNS timeouts and TCP retransmits when hitting your peering endpoint in us-west-2.

We need an urgent triage — can you confirm whether there were any peering changes, firewall or proxy maintenance on your end this morning? We're escalating internally and can hop on a call.

Attachments: oxfordlane_trace_summary.tar.gz (pcap + summary)

-Maya
Maya Allen
SRE Lead, Oxford Lane
maya.allen@oxfordlane.com

- Kim: can you coordinate CS comms if we need to escalate to execs / propose a credit?

Subject: Re: Fwd: Latency/5xx spike starting ~08:45 PST - checkout failures

On Fri, Apr 5, 2029 at 09:28 Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Forwarding Oxford Lane's alert — they attached a pcap and see DNS timeouts + retransmits hitting our us-west-2 peering endpoint.

I've pulled flow logs and run a quick egress path trace. Preliminary notes below (summary attached as egres_path_trace.png):

- No planned maintenance on our peering fabric during the window. However, I see sudden increase in SYN retransmits and DNS query retries targeting peer IP 52.204.11.77 (Oxford's advertised peer) starting 08:42 PST.
- The path asymmetry shows our egress through proxy-rcx-5 (owned by our partner transit provider) for ~10% of flows, while baseline uses proxy-rcx-2. RCX-5 shows elevated queueing (p95 egress latency +320ms) and packet drops concurrent with the customer's traces.
- DNS timeouts: our edge resolvers are forwarding for some hostnames with TTLs that recently dropped; combined with transient packet loss this produced repeated client-side retries and increased end-to-end tail latency.

Immediate mitigations I've pushed (effective now):
1) Forced route override for Oxford Lane CIDR to prefer rcx-2 (fallback path) — should reduce tail latency for most traffic within 3–5min.
2) Increased local DNS cache TTL for their hostnames to 30s to reduce query volume while we stabilize.
3) Enabled aggressive TCP retransmit backoff tuning on the egress proxies to reduce bursts of retransmits (temporary).

Next steps:
- We'll continue to monitor the reroute and provide a 15m update. If queueing persists on rcx-5 we'll request partner to throttle/shed non-critical flows.
- Engineering to coordinate an RCA with the transit provider and Oxford Lane's network team.

Note on customer comms: Rafael, please let Oxford Lane know we have a mitigation in place and we're tracking for improvement. If the issue persists beyond 1 hour we should offer a formal incident review and consider a goodwill credit per DL-4821.

Attachments: egress_path_trace.png

-Vanessa Ortiz
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

On Fri, Apr 5, 2029 at 10:04 Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Immediate mitigations I've pushed (effective now):
> 1) Forced route override for Oxford Lane CIDR to prefer rcx-2 …

Oxford Lane — looped in Eli per Rafael's request. Quick summary and plan for execs: 

Summary:
- Customer observed sudden tail-latency and 5xx starting 2029-04-05 08:45 PST. Our telemetry showed asymmetric egress routing where a small subset of flows hit a congested partner proxy (rcx-5), causing packet loss and DNS retry amplification.
- Mitigations applied (reroute + TTL bump + TCP tuning) reduced error rate from ~6% to ~0.4% and brought median latency back toward baseline; some tail outliers persisted for flows that still traversed rcx-5.

Action items (owners & timeline):
- Ops (Vanessa): continue monitoring and keep route override until transit partner confirms queueing cleared. (Now → +6 hours)
- Network Eng (Marissa): coordinate RCA with transit partner and provide a draft incident report within 48 hours. (Marissa lead)
- CS (Rafael/Kim): schedule a customer-facing incident review and offer a goodwill credit if the final impact exceeds SLA thresholds. Draft comms by EOD. (Rafael lead)
- Exec sync: 11:00 AM PT tomorrow to brief on potential impact to committed revenue and discuss any contractual remediation.

Customer message (to send now):
Rafael — please use this template: apologise briefly, say mitigations are applied, confirm we are monitoring and schedule incident review. Offer immediate workaround and next steps.

I'll draft the incident notification and exec note. Rafael — please confirm you have the customer's permission to share the pcap with our transit partner (we will need it for the RCA).

-Kim
